{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey there, what's going on today?
seeker: Hello. It is a fine day, how about yourself?
supporter: It really is! I am just taking in the fresh air in the backyard. 
seeker: That is awesome.
supporter: Thanks! What is going on in your neck of the woods? 
seeker: Sort of stuck inside trying to make a dime but it is alright.
supporter: Yeah great minds think alike.. do you do anything else for work? 
seeker: Looking for a good job right now.
seeker: I wanted to talk about a personal issue I have been having, though.
supporter: Okay, you know I'm here for you. Talk to me, what's happening? 
seeker: My father and I had a fight 2 years ago and haven't spoke since.
supporter: The same happened to me, and then my father passed away. If there is anything I can say, is to swallow pride and cherish the moments you have on earth together. What was the fight over?
seeker: Yeah I am afraid that these things can happen. It was only over material things.
supporter: That was my next question, what the fight was over. Do you think he would be open to mending things? 
seeker: It is weird because I called him out for being manipulative so this is his defense. 
supporter: Usually when people feel singled out, they only have a few mechanisms. Unfortunately, most people tend to run away instead of fixing things. It tends to be the easier option. 
seeker: I would likely take advantage of an opportunity to be the bigger person.
supporter: When you try to fix things, just remember that this is his method. I wouldn't hold back on what you have to say, but just word it so that he doesn't feel the need to flee. 
seeker: That is probably decent advice.
supporter: It is HIS responsibility as a parent to want to fix things, but you are also being the bigger person here. I applaud you and hope that he is receptive. 
seeker: I hope so too, but the opportunity seems tenuous 
supporter: How did you guys leave it? 
seeker: Threatening and disparagement haha
supporter: Ha, well after two years, feelings had to have changed. Even a little. Does he live nearby?
seeker: Yeah someday. I think I will have to try you know. THanks for the advice.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
Hey there, what's going on today?
Hello. It is a fine day, how about yourself?
It really is! I am just taking in the fresh air in the backyard.
That is awesome.
Thanks! What is going on in your neck of the woods?
Sort of stuck inside trying to make a dime but it is alright.
Yeah great minds think alike.. do you do anything else for work?
Looking for a good job right now.
I wanted to talk about a personal issue I have been having, though.
Okay, you know I'm here for you. Talk to me, what's happening?
My father and I had a fight 2 years ago and haven't spoke since.
The same happened to me, and then my father passed away. If there is anything I can say, is to swallow pride and cherish the moments you have on earth together. What was the fight over?
Yeah I am afraid that these things can happen. It was only over material things.
That was my next question, what the fight was over. Do you think he would be open to mending things?
It is weird because I called him out for being manipulative so this is his defense.
Usually when people feel singled out, they only have a few mechanisms. Unfortunately, most people tend to run away instead of fixing things. It tends to be the easier option.
I would likely take advantage of an opportunity to be the bigger person.
When you try to fix things, just remember that this is his method. I wouldn't hold back on what you have to say, but just word it so that he doesn't feel the need to flee.
That is probably decent advice.
It is HIS responsibility as a parent to want to fix things, but you are also being the bigger person here. I applaud you and hope that he is receptive.
I hope so too, but the opportunity seems tenuous
How did you guys leave it?
Threatening and disparagement haha
Ha, well after two years, feelings had to have changed. Even a little. Does he live nearby?
Yeah someday. I think I will have to try you know. THanks for the advice.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I really needed to talk to someone today.
supporter: Of course, Charles. I’m here for you. What’s on your mind?
seeker: I just got the news today that I’m losing my job. It's really shaken me.
supporter: I’m so sorry to hear that. It must be incredibly tough. How do you feel about it all?
seeker: I feel lost, to be honest. The financial pressures were already hard on us, and now without my income, I don’t know how we’ll manage.
supporter: That’s a lot to handle, especially after everything you’ve been dealing with recently. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed.
seeker: Yeah, and I’m worried about telling Margaret. She’s just started feeling stable with her new job, and I don’t want to add more stress.
supporter: It's commendable that you’re thinking about her feelings, but you're in this together. Sometimes sharing burdens can make them a bit easier to bear.
seeker: That's true. I just hate the idea of disappointing her or my daughter Emily. They rely on me so much.
supporter: It sounds like you feel a deep sense of responsibility for your family. And it’s okay to feel that way, but remember you’re human too.
seeker: I know. I've been telling myself I have to be the strong one ever since Emily was in the hospital. Every issue seems bigger now.
supporter: You've been strong through a lot of stressful situations, Charles. Taking care of yourself is also a part of being strong for your family.
seeker: You're right. I haven't really been taking the time to address how I'm feeling. I've just been pushing it aside.
supporter: Would it help to talk about what lies ahead? Maybe work through some practical steps or support you might need?
seeker: That might help. I guess the first step is talking to Margaret, although I feel so anxious.
supporter: It's natural to feel anxious, but you have a strong partnership. She might have solutions or support to offer, and being open can strengthen your relationship.
seeker: She’s been my rock through all of this. I do trust her, and I need to remember that.
supporter: Trust is so important, and it seems like you’ve both navigated many challenges together before. Remember, you’re not alone in this.
seeker: Thank you for the reminder. Even when things feel heavy, it’s good to know I have people I can turn to.
supporter: Always, Charles. Reaching out today was a brave step, and I hope it’s provided some clarity or solace.
seeker: It has, more than I expected. I’ll try to take things one day at a time and lean on my support system when I need to.

Hi! It seems someone in the family is having sleeping issues. Correct me if I am wrong
My daughter is really sick and its causing her to have trouble sleeping.  Not sure what to do.
Sorry to here about it. It must be hard for you to see her in trouble.
May I ask What happen to her.
It is.  She's miserable, and it's causing us to not sleep as well.
It's nothing serious, common cold, but she has asthma so whenever she gets sick, it causes labored breathing.
I can feel how stressed you are right now but she will recover fast.
I know she will, I always lack sleep whenever she's not feeling well.  I wish I could be sick for her.
When my kid have cold, I nebulize her and later it make her sleep well

Really, I'll have to try that. Thank you!

Thank you so much.  You have been very helpful.
I feel much better after talking with you.
I hope you have a good rest of the day.
Mt best wishes are there with you. Be positive she will sleep well and recover soon.
I will. And I pray that she will.

Hey Charles, I'm here for you. How are you holding up after everything with Emily?
Hi, it's been really challenging. Seeing Emily in the hospital is something no parent wants.
I completely understand. It must be really hard to see her go through this. How is she doing now?
She's stable now, thankfully. But every time she has an episode, it takes a toll on us, especially Margaret.
I'm relieved to hear Emily is stable. The stress must be immense for you both. What's been the most difficult part?
I think it's the feeling of helplessness. We do everything we can, but it feels like we're just waiting for the next attack.
That sounds overwhelming, Charles. Feeling helpless is tough. Have you found anything that helps ease that feeling, even a little?
Talking to someone helps a bit. And knowing we're following the doctor’s advice, but the uncertainty lingers.
It's good that you're reaching out and following medical guidance. It's okay to feel uncertain; anyone would in your shoes.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Margaret tries to be strong for Emily, but I can see it's wearing her down too.
Margaret sounds like a wonderful mother, but it's important for both of you to care for yourselves too. How are you supporting each other?
We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.
That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.
Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.
That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?
I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.
Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.
Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.
You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.
It sounds like you and Margaret are doing an incredible job under tough circumstances. Keep leaning on each other. You're not alone.
Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things out and know someone understands.
Anytime, Charles. I'm here whenever you need to talk. You're doing great, just keep taking those steps forward.

documents.text: Hey, I've been going through a lot lately and could really use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
Well, I've made a big decision to cut down on my working hours.
That's a significant step. How are you feeling about it?
It's a mix of relief and uncertainty. I'm glad to have more time for myself, but I worry about my career.
It's completely normal to feel both relieved and anxious. Taking care of your mental health is crucial though.
You're right. I've been trying to focus more on painting, as it helps with my stress.
That's wonderful. Engaging in a hobby can be so therapeutic. Have you noticed any changes in how you feel since you started painting?

Hi there. What academic pressures are troubling you today?

ya it does help

Hi! How are you tonight?
I've been better. I just buried my dog yesterday
She was going to turn 15 next month
Ouch! I'm so sorry to hear that. I never lost a dog, but I've lost cats.
Is 14 a good age for a dog?
I have my first dog so I don't know much, he is 9 years old and came with our house.
Actually, yes. She was old and had dementia.
The oldest dog I evet had was 15
I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us.
How did your dog come with the house?

Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? We moved from FL to KY and the little dog just hung out here, he really belonged to the neighbor's son who didn't want him, so he just ran around wild and wouldn't leave. I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.
I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.
I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2
Thank you. that means a lot
We both had dogs when we met.
So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol

I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it!
They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes
I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.
I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.
Thanks. Another person who has pets helps
They understand

I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.

I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog.
Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.
Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed.
That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.
I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D
You too. Thanks so much. bye

I have one more thing to say - wise words from this 92 year old lady at church named Sue. She told me this after my brother died. When you get older, everyone you know is practically dead.  She said "Life is for the living, if you get caught up to much in all the death, you won't life."  True words. God bless, have a good night.

documents.text: Hey, I just need someone to talk to.
Hi Amanda, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I decided to start painting as a hobby, but it's starting to stress me out.
That sounds tough. Picking up something new should be relaxing. What's stressing you about it?
I guess I put a lot of pressure on myself to be good at it right away. It's supposed to be fun, but I just feel like I'm failing.
It's understandable to want to excel, Amanda. Remember, it's okay not to be perfect. It's about the process, right?
Yeah, I know. It's just hard not to get competitive with myself. And with everything else going on, it feels like I need to be good at something.
I get that. You've been dealing with a lot, especially with work and your relationships. How has painting been helping you otherwise?
Well, for a while, it did help shift my mind away from work and personal stress. I kind of get lost in the colors and strokes. But then I start criticizing myself.
Criticism can be so draining. Sometimes our own expectations create more stress. Have you tried just painting without any goals in mind?
I haven't really. I always set a goal, maybe from habit because of work. But I think I'll try just playing around with it.
That sounds like a great idea. Letting go of expectations could bring back some joy and relaxation to it.
Yeah, I'll give it a shot. I could use some light-heartedness right now.
That's the spirit! Remember, it's okay to just enjoy the moment without judgment.
Thanks. It's just been a rough patch with everything, work, and Bill... And then my ex...
It sounds like you have a full plate. Dealing with all those emotions about Bill and your ex can be really challenging.
It is. Sometimes I just miss Bill, and seeing my ex with someone else hit me harder than I expected. I'm trying not to let it affect me, but sometimes it just hurts.
Heart matters can be so complex. It's important to give yourself time and space to feel those emotions. Healing isn't linear.
You're right. I think painting was supposed to be a distraction, but maybe I need to let myself feel without distraction sometimes.
Yes, allowing yourself to feel is part of the healing process. Balance between distraction and reflection can be helpful.
I'm going to try to be kinder to myself and let go of the pressure. Maybe then painting will just be painting.
That sounds like a positive step forward, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed to talk about all this. I feel a bit lighter now.

I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.

It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to
tough it out.

That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.

I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.

Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
You are welcome.  I wish you well.
I think I have a few tools now to make things better.

Hi there, how is this season treating you?
It's alright. Definitely not as cold as last year which is something to be slightly thankful for.
Well let's be grateful for small mercies :). How are you feeling in yourself though? Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
I'm worried about grad school
Ah I am sorry to hear that. Please try not to worry too much as it's a common worry to have. Do you want to tell me the details?

Sure. One of my classes is extremely difficult and the professor has not been responsive at all. The TA is kind enough to make time to help me with homework, but my grades are still not great. It makes me feel really dumb and undeserving to be in that class
So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?

I want to be in the program, it's just that I feel like everyone is so much smarter than me and my performance in that class makes me question my admission into the programs sometimes. When I feel like this after submitting homework, I end up crying because I just want to do well. I enjoy this field, just not this  class in particular.
I'm afraid of failing, but I'm not sure if that should be a concern either. Over the past 3 years, no one has gotten a grade lower than a B.
But do you really think that you would have been admitted to the class if you were not up to the standard? Do you think that maybe most of your classmates are secretly feeling the same?
Sometimes I think about that. At the same time, I feel like it's unfair to compare myself to others.
This sounds like it might be a self esteem issue and not about your grades. I have felt this sort of thing myself and I do know how awful it is to be so hard on yourself.
So what do I do about it? I don't want to keep feeling like this
Have you thought about seeing a therapist? Does your school have any free therapy programmes you could use?

I don't think my school has free therapy programs. I have thought about seeing a therapist but I've heard therapy is very expensive.With student loans, I didn't really put much more research into therapy past hearing about the costs.
A far as I am aware there are charitable organisations which can arrange a few free therapy session for you. Perhaps you could talk to your doctor about it?
I have had free therapy sessions before and I found them very helpful
I think free therapy sessions would be a good place to start
It would help you work on your self confidence and you might find that you are not doing as badly in school as you think you are.
Yeah, there are definitely a lot of other things i'm insecure about
Then I think it is probably just a general self esteem issue and nothing academic!
Anyway it's been really nice to talk to you and I hope that everything goes your way
I think talking about this has helped. I'll do a little more digging. Thank you!
You're most welcome, have a lovely Holiday season.

That sounds really stressful. It must be tough feeling like your efforts aren't recognized.
Yeah, exactly. I'm trying to help as much as I can, especially with work being so demanding.

I just feel overwhelmed sometimes. I want to be there for my family but also need to take care of myself.

I know, but it's hard to shake off. I want things to be okay between Lily and me.

I've been thinking of reaching out and talking it over calmly. I don't want this to become a bigger issue.

I hope so. I just hate being in this kind of conflict. It feels exhausting.

Thanks for saying that. I guess I'll try to focus on the good side of it.

Yeah, he's been amazing. I think I'll talk to him more about how I'm feeling too.

documents.text: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly! What's on your mind?
I just found out that I didn't get the scholarship I applied for.
I'm so sorry to hear that. You must be really disappointed.
Yeah, it's just frustrating. I really thought this would be my chance to ease some of the financial pressures of grad school.
I can imagine. It's tough when you're expecting something that could make life a bit easier and it doesn't come through.
Exactly. And it just feels like a setback after working so hard, especially after everything with my thesis.
You've been through a lot recently, with the criticism on your thesis and the group project issues. It's okay to feel upset about this.
Thanks. I guess I just keep thinking about all the time and effort I put into the application. It feels like it's always something.
Your dedication is amazing, Kelly. Even if this didn’t work out, it doesn’t take away from all the effort you’ve put in.
It's hard to keep that perspective when these things happen back to back. It just adds to feeling stuck, you know?
Absolutely, and it's important to acknowledge that feeling. Have you thought about what you might do next?
I'm trying to keep my options open. There's the internship offer, but I'm not sure about committing to it right now.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. The internship could be a valuable experience, but it's okay to take your time deciding.
I appreciate you saying that. I guess I'll think on it more after this initial disappointment passes.
That's a healthy approach, Kelly. It's important to give yourself space to process everything.
Thanks for listening and for understanding. It's comforting to have someone to talk to about this.

documents.text: Hey, I hope you're available to chat for a bit. I could use some support right now.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, I finally told my colleague that I have feelings for him, and we decided to start dating.
That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.
It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?
I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.
Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?
I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.
It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?
Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.
That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?
Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.
That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?
My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.
It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?
I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.
That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?
I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.

I'm just feeling sad and depressed over the breakup that I described above. Hoping for some inspiration.

I feel so betrayed. I was completely caught off guard. Now I don't know what to do with myself.
When did this happen, How long ago
Just this last week. I came home from work early Thursday. I guess I should have texted first so he could get rid of the guy. Or maybe not. Maybe it's better that I found out.
So you had been together for awhile and all of  a sudden he has another person in his life
We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.
Was this guy an associate of yours as well
So basically this guy was a stranger that you know of.
Yes that's right, I'd never seen him before.
Did you have any children between you
No, it was just the two of us. And two cats. Who are still here with me. There's that at least.
DiId your partner work also
Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.
Maybe the time on his hands enabled to him meet someone while you were working. Did he have a following that you knew of
has there been habits like this before

Maybe it did. There are some fans of his work on social media, and he's on all the popular social media sights. I don't know if he me the guy online or what. There hasn't been anything like this before that I know of. Maybe there was. I trusted him and didn't look at his messages or anything.
His actions none the less are not right
Do you have an idea his websites
No, they weren't, I agree there. He took all his devices with him. I can see his stuff from a user point of view, like anyone else in the public could, but nothing of his personal stuff.
The fact that he cheated on you and I assume you broke up with him is hard
He must have a special account that people can access to, can you possibly find it out
Yeah, we're over. And it is hard. I'll get past it I suppose. I don't think I could, but I don't really want to anyway at this point. It's not going to help us get back together or anything.
Maybe you need to focus on you now, and plan your days ahead.
I think you're right. Just look forward.
Had you known before hand it might be of help, but the sudden impact does not make it any better
if you look back you will have regrets. If you look forward you will see a future
You're right. Thank you for listening. I feel a little better already. I'll get through this. Me and the cats :-)
Take a cup of coffee, sit and write your thoughts then burn them
Sounds like a good plan.
Write your past down then throw it into a fire
Thank you again. I'm going to go ahead and wrap up the conversation. I'll be okay.
OK. Have a blessed night.
You too. Take care.

documents.text: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.

That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?

It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?

You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.

That's wonderful! How has painting been for you?
It's been surprisingly soothing. There's something calming about watching the colors blend on the canvas. I didn't realize how much I needed this creative outlet.
It's amazing how art can have that effect. Do you find it helps with some of the stress from work and your personal life?
Definitely. Work has been overwhelming, especially after that meeting with my new boss. Painting helps me disconnect for a while.
I'm really glad to hear that it's providing a little escape. Has it also helped with your feelings of anxiety and the challenges you're facing with Jack?
In a way, yes. With Jack, things are still a bit rocky. We both need our space, but we also want to be there for each other. It's a delicate balance.
Balancing independence and intimacy can be tough. It's great you're aware of it and working through it. Have you been able to talk openly with Jack about this?
We've talked a bit. It's hard to navigate sometimes, but we're trying to communicate more clearly. I guess painting gives me time to reflect on my feelings before discussing them.
That's really insightful, Sarah. It sounds like you're using painting as a way to process your emotions, which is so healthy.

It's understandable to feel that way after everything you've been through at work. Do you think painting might help in building your confidence to handle these challenges?
I think it might. It's building my patience and giving me a sense of accomplishment, even if it's small. Maybe I can apply that mindset at work too.
Absolutely, every small victory counts. And you've achieved so much by just starting to paint. What have you enjoyed painting the most so far?
I love painting landscapes. They remind me of places I'd like to see if I ever get around to taking that vacation my therapist suggested.
That's a beautiful way to plan and dream. Maybe these paintings can be the first step towards that vacation, a visual diary of where you want to go.
That's a lovely thought. I like it. Maybe painting these places will give me the courage to one day explore them in real life.
I'd love to hear about your travels when they happen. For now, I'm here if you ever want to share more of your art journey or anything else.
Thank you for listening and being here. It means a lot to know I have support while I figure things out.
Anytime, Sarah. Keep painting and taking small steps. You're doing great.

documents.text: Hey there, do you have a moment? I really need someone to talk to.
Of course, Kelly! What's going on?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed at my internship. It's starting to feel like too much.
I'm sorry to hear that. What about it is overwhelming you?
It's just the workload is intense, and I feel like I'm constantly behind. It's affecting my confidence.
That sounds incredibly tough. It's understandable to feel that way with so much on your plate.

Managing both grad school and an internship is incredibly challenging. How have you been coping so far?

I hadn't thought about that. Maybe I can propose a solution rather than keeping it all in.

Hi there, how is this season treating you?
It's alright. Definitely not as cold as last year which is something to be slightly thankful for.
Well let's be grateful for small mercies :). How are you feeling in yourself though? Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
I'm worried about grad school
Ah I am sorry to hear that. Please try not to worry too much as it's a common worry to have. Do you want to tell me the details?

Sure. One of my classes is extremely difficult and the professor has not been responsive at all. The TA is kind enough to make time to help me with homework, but my grades are still not great. It makes me feel really dumb and undeserving to be in that class
So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?

I want to be in the program, it's just that I feel like everyone is so much smarter than me and my performance in that class makes me question my admission into the programs sometimes. When I feel like this after submitting homework, I end up crying because I just want to do well. I enjoy this field, just not this  class in particular.
I'm afraid of failing, but I'm not sure if that should be a concern either. Over the past 3 years, no one has gotten a grade lower than a B.
But do you really think that you would have been admitted to the class if you were not up to the standard? Do you think that maybe most of your classmates are secretly feeling the same?
Sometimes I think about that. At the same time, I feel like it's unfair to compare myself to others.
This sounds like it might be a self esteem issue and not about your grades. I have felt this sort of thing myself and I do know how awful it is to be so hard on yourself.
So what do I do about it? I don't want to keep feeling like this
Have you thought about seeing a therapist? Does your school have any free therapy programmes you could use?

I don't think my school has free therapy programs. I have thought about seeing a therapist but I've heard therapy is very expensive.With student loans, I didn't really put much more research into therapy past hearing about the costs.
A far as I am aware there are charitable organisations which can arrange a few free therapy session for you. Perhaps you could talk to your doctor about it?
I have had free therapy sessions before and I found them very helpful
I think free therapy sessions would be a good place to start
It would help you work on your self confidence and you might find that you are not doing as badly in school as you think you are.
Yeah, there are definitely a lot of other things i'm insecure about
Then I think it is probably just a general self esteem issue and nothing academic!
Anyway it's been really nice to talk to you and I hope that everything goes your way
I think talking about this has helped. I'll do a little more digging. Thank you!
You're most welcome, have a lovely Holiday season.

documents.text: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
Hello? Anyone there?
Hi sorry
I'm having trouble getting motivated to finish my senior thesis
Ah! I remember my thesis, a lot of work. One thing for certain, I have a lot of pride over my accomplishment, it was well worth it. When is it due?
In about a month.
I'm sure you will be able to finish it, sometimes we find ourselves in a slump and need some fresh air blown our way.
Do you have an advisor who is holding you accountable?
Yes, but I've been really bad about keeping her in the loop. I feel bad when I fall behind, and then I'm fearful of getting back in touch with her.

Whenever I have a large project and lose motivation, I set my goals on paper, then break it down into smaller bites. For example, I will make sure I work one hour on certain days, or call a friend, I generate ideas to keep me on track.

Yes, I sometimes feel guilty and then don't want to face the music, but actually the best thing to do is recognize you are NOT the first person she knows that got behind. So she is surely experienced with people who need some encouragement. She is the BEST person to go to, actually.
That sounds like a good idea regarding putting it down on paper.

It has always helped me. For example, you can break it down into 4 weeks, then each week write your goals -- maybe put call Advisor or go stop by every week, but I would put that first for the first week.

Then as you check off items, you will see you are moving, even if at a snail's pace, you are moving, and that always encourages me. Sometimes I do not realize how much I AM doing, until I see it on paper. Paper doesn't lie, but my emotions sometimes cloud my thinking.
My other problem is that I'm a perfectionist. I tend to over-analyze and get bogged down, especially when doing research.
Another idea is rewards, when you finish one goal, perhaps put a reward for yourself,  a yogurt with sprinkles or something like that
You sound like me! I had to learn that I need to strive for EXCELLENCE, not perfection. Perfection will drain us. Do the best I can, leave the rest to God.

That is why a time line is good. For example, you make a goal that you will work on your reference and citation page for one hour, after that, you are DONE, If you have time at the end, you can revisit it. The hour is my suggestion, you make your own. lol THAT way, you don't get caught going on and on for 6 hours to make it perfect. One hour is reasonable.
That definitely sounds reasonable. Putting micro deadlines in might be what I need to do to keep me focused.

I do this with EVERYTHING in life because I tend to go on and on too focused and lose track of everything. lol For example, I clean each room for 15 minutes a week. If it needs more, I do more, but I set the timer and you would be surprised how well that works, otherwise, I will spend all my time perfecting one room and the rest is a mess.
Also, your Advisor will know tips to help you too. She has advised a lot of people, her objectivity and experience can give get RIGHT to the heart of any problem, quickly too.
My advisor is a tough woman, I'm not going to beat around the bush. She tends to make everything miserable.

Hello. How are you feeling today?
Hi, I'm feeling really anxious today.
What has made you feel anxious?
Yesterday my company laid off 10% of the workforce and another 10% got furloughed.
I'm afraid I might be in the next round.
I am very sorry to hear that. I am currently in a situation where furloughs are greatly affecting my family as well.
Oh no that's terrible.
The problem is, I am right now the only breadwinner in the family. My wife was laid off three months ago
Are you given specifics on time of furlough?
No, it's basically until things get better.
I know that's very difficult. And no doubt why you're here working for crumbs.
It's why I'm here as well.
Yeah, trying to make ends meet wherever I can
I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also
I know it's a difficult time. Yes Uber is definitely overrun right now. Have you taken any time out to address your anxiety so it doesn't become more serious?
I don't know what I can do. I've been trying to keep busy. And I can't afford a therapist or anything like that.
Yes, that's definitely an expense you can't afford right now. But are you familiar with the concept of controlled breathing to help reduce or relieve anxiety?
Like meditation?
What am I supposed to do? Just breathe in and out a lot?

Not exactly. Controlled breathing is more of getting yourself into a quiet room. Closing your eyes, and purposely and intently focusing on your breathing. Slowly breathe in for a count of 5, then slowly exhale for a count of 5. Repeat this process for approximately 10 minute. It will help your stress levels and help regulate your heart rate!
Oh I didn't know that. No, I haven't tried that. Does it really work?
I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.
ok I can try it I guess
thanks for that tip
No problem. I hope this gives you some relief! Stay strong!
yeah, thanks. same to you

My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.
That's helpful. Thanks.
No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.
Thanks. You too

I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.

Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.

You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.

documents.text: Hey, can I vent about something?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I just found out I missed out on the overseas promotion I was offered a while back.
Oh no, that's really disappointing, especially after having been offered it. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I feel a bit betrayed. No one even told me; I just found out through the grapevine.
That sounds really tough, Jane. It's hard to be left out of the loop like that. How are you coping with all these emotions?
I'm trying to process it, but it's hard not to feel like it's a reflection of my value at work.
It's understandable to feel that way. Your work and contributions are valuable, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. Do you want to talk more about what led to this?
I think it's a combination of things. There was so much going on—my anxiety, all the financial stress, and then this on top of it.
It's a lot to deal with, for sure. It reminds me of when you were considering the promotion and feeling overwhelmed. Do you think those feelings had an impact?
Maybe. I was really torn about the decision, fearing how it would affect my relationship with Eliza and just leaving everything behind.
It's such a big decision with lots of factors to weigh. It makes sense that it took a toll on you. How are you feeling about your relationship with Eliza now, after everything?
We’ve been better. We managed to patch things up after the wedding planning fallout, but I wonder how she’d have reacted if I moved.
It sounds like your bond with her is important to you. Maybe those fears were valid, but it's good to hear you've reconciled. How do you see your career moving forward after this setback?
It's hard to say. I feel stuck, but in some ways, relieved I don't have to move overseas. Yet, there's this nagging fear I'll remain stagnant in my career.
